stem: A client is collecting a 24-hour urine specimen for urinary free cortisol. Which statement requires follow-up before submission?

options.A: I collected urine throughout the prescribed 24 hours.
options.B: I missed one morning void but collected all the others.
options.C: I followed the laboratory's preservative and storage instructions.
options.D: I recorded the collection duration and total urine volume.

rationale: Mayo Clinic Laboratories states that improper 24-hour urinary free cortisol collection can alter results; a missed morning collection may cause a false-negative result and collection beyond 24 hours may cause a false-positive result. Thus B indicates an incomplete, potentially unreliable specimen and requires follow-up. A, C, and D reflect required or appropriate collection elements. The nurse should follow laboratory/facility procedure rather than assume a universal restart rule.
educational_objective: Recognize that a missed void can invalidate or distort a 24-hour urine result and requires follow-up before submission.
source_locator: Necessary Information: 24-hour volume required. Specimen Required > Collection Instructions: collect urine for 24 hours; follow specified preservative instructions. Cautions: improper collection may alter results; missed morning collection may cause false-negative testing; extra morning collection (>24 hours) may cause false-positive testing.
source_claim_supported: Completeness and timing are necessary for valid 24-hour urinary free cortisol measurement; a missed morning void can falsely lower diagnostic interpretation.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Printed page 13, Reduction of Risk Potential: obtain specimens other than blood for diagnostic testing; monitor diagnostic testing/results; educate clients about treatments/procedures.
blueprint_topic: Reduction of Risk Potential — diagnostic specimen collection/preanalytic error
correction_summary: Replaced the vague generic purpose-of-24-hour-urine item with a test-specific specimen-validity scenario supported by Mayo's explicit missed-collection caution.
audit_findings: Mayo directly supports the collection interval, required volume, handling and false-negative risk from a missed morning void. B alone creates a documented validity problem; A/C/D are appropriate. No universal restart rule, threshold or generic handling claim remains. Blueprint directly matches NCSBN 2026 specimen collection. Independent adversarial second pass found no second answer, cueing, ambiguity or unresolved conflict.

final_reaudit_scope: Mayo CORTU validity/cautions; NCSBN 2026 specimen collection; A-D and adversarial review
